q: Ajax's ground took the name Johan Cruijff ArenA at the start of which season?
sub: Announced on 5 April 2018, two years after Cruyff died.
note: Duplicate. The shipping row "What was the Johan Cruijff ArenA called before it was renamed in 2018?" already carries the 2018 renaming, so this asks the same fact back to front. The sub was wrong as well: the name was announced 25 April 2017 and the logo revealed 25 April 2018, not 5 April.

q: In which Dutch city would you find De Grolsch Veste?
sub: FC Twente have played there since it opened in 1998.
note: Enschede and the 1998 opening confirmed on the stadium article. Sub reworded: it named the Arke Stadion, which is the answer to a shipping question.

q: In which Dutch city would you find the Rat Verlegh Stadion?
sub: NAC have played there since 1996.
note: Breda and NAC moving in for 1996 confirmed on the stadium article.

q: In which Dutch town would you find the Mandemakers Stadion?
sub: RKC moved in when it opened in 1996.
note: Waalwijk and RKC moving in when it opened in 1996 confirmed.

q: In which Limburg town would you find the Parkstad Limburg Stadion?
sub: Roda JC moved in when it opened in August 2000.
note: Duplicate. Mirror image of the shipping row "Which Kerkrade ground did Roda JC leave in 2000 for the Parkstad Limburg Stadion?", which hands over both the town and the stadium.

q: The Fortuna Sittard Stadion opened in 1999. In which Dutch province does it stand?
sub: Built on an industrial site for 30 million guilders.
note: Opened 14 November 1999, Sittard is in Limburg, and the 30 million guilder cost is on the stadium article.

q: Which club from The Hague plays at the ground known since 2022 as the Bingoal Stadion?
sub: The same ground was the Kyocera Stadion and then the Cars Jeans Stadion.
note: Duplicate of the shipping easy row "Which Dutch club plays its home games in The Hague?", same answer with the city given away. Also a stale live fact: the ground has been the WerkTalent Stadion since 2025, not the Bingoal Stadion.

q: Which Dutch club has played at De Adelaarshorst in Deventer since 1920?
sub: The name means the eagle's nest.
note: Go Ahead at the Vetkampstraat ground since 1920 confirmed, and Adelaarshorst does mean eagle's nest.

q: Which Dutch club moved into the new Kooi Stadion in Leeuwarden in 2024?
sub: They opened it on 18 August 2024 with a 1-0 defeat by Helmond Sport.
note: Kooi Stadion opened 18 August 2024 with a 1-0 defeat by Helmond Sport, confirmed.

q: Which software company's name went onto AZ's stadium in 2010, after the DSB name came off?
sub: For one season in between it was simply the AZ Stadion.
note: DSB 2006 to 2009, AZ Stadion 2009 to 2010, AFAS from 2010, all confirmed.

q: Which Dutch club left the Oosterenkstadion for a new ground that opened in 2009?
sub: They were called FC Zwolle at the time.
note: PEC left the Oosterenk for the ground that opened on 29 August 2009, and were FC Zwolle at the time.

q: Which Dutch club's ground staged the 2017 Women's European Championship final?
sub: De Grolsch Veste, 28,182 in, and the Netherlands beat Denmark.
note: The 2017 Women's Euro final was at De Grolsch Veste, 28,182 in, Netherlands beat Denmark 4-2.

q: Which cleaning company's name went onto Heracles Almelo's ground in 2019, replacing Polman?
sub: First as Erve Asito, then plain Asito Stadion from 2024.
note: Asito, an Almelo cleaning company, took the naming rights on 1 July 2019 from Polman, Erve Asito then Asito Stadion from 2024.

q: Which Dutch club's new ground opened in 1996 under the name Fujifilm Stadium?
sub: It became the Mycom Stadium in 2003 and the Rat Verlegh Stadion in 2006.
note: Opened in 1996 as the Fujifilm Stadium, Mycom 2003, Rat Verlegh 2006, all confirmed.

q: Ajax played their last match at De Meer in April 1996. Which club were the visitors?
sub: 28 April 1996, after 62 years in the ground.
note: Last match at De Meer on 28 April 1996 against Willem II, after 62 years, confirmed.

q: In which year did De Kuip become an all-seater, cutting its capacity to about 51,000?
sub: The roof was extended over every stand at the same time.
note: All-seater after the 1994 rebuild at 51,117 seats, confirmed.

q: PSV set a Philips Stadion attendance record in September 2015 against which English club?
sub: 35,292 in for the Champions League tie on 15 September 2015.
note: 35,292 against Manchester United on 15 September 2015 is the stadium record on the English article.

q: Which member of the Dutch royal family opened the Amsterdam ArenA in August 1996?
sub: 14 August 1996, three years after building started.
note: Queen Beatrix opened it on 14 August 1996, confirmed.

q: Which Amsterdam ground hosted the 1962 European Cup final, Benfica against Real Madrid?
sub: Benfica won 5-3 with Eusebio scoring twice.
note: Benfica beat Real Madrid 5-3 in the 1962 European Cup final at the Olympisch Stadion, Eusebio scored twice.

q: Which English club beat AZ 3-0 in the opening match at their new Alkmaar stadium in August 2006?
sub: Gilberto Silva scored the first goal in the ground.
note: Arsenal won the opening match 3-0 on 4 August 2006 with Gilberto Silva scoring the ground's first goal.

q: Part of a Dutch stadium roof collapsed during building work in July 2011, killing two men. Which ground?
sub: Two workers were killed and fourteen hurt when the new stand's roof came down.
note: Roof collapse on 7 July 2011 during work on the new stand, two workers killed and fourteen injured, all confirmed. Sub replaced: the claim that Twente played on roofless while the inquiry ran is not in the source.

q: Excelsior's Rotterdam ground has a stand named after which striker, who trained there as a boy?
sub: He was at Woudestein from 1997 to 1999 before Feyenoord.
note: The stand named after Robin van Persie and his 1997 to 1999 spell in the Excelsior youth are both on the stadium article.

q: NAC Breda's ground carried the names Fujifilm and Mycom before 2006. Whose name did it take then?
sub: NAC's most famous player, and the man the club still names its ground after.
note: Fujifilm 1996 to 2003, Mycom 2003 to 2006, Rat Verlegh from 2006, all confirmed. Pulled from hard to normal: the ground is universally called the Rat Verlegh Stadion, so the name is the answer.

q: MVV Maastricht's ground De Geusselt takes its name from what nearby building?
sub: The park around the ground carries the same name.
note: The Dutch article says in as many words that the ground is named after the nearby Kasteel Geusselt, so this is a documented origin, not a story.

q: Which Maastricht ground did MVV leave in 1961 when De Geusselt opened?
sub: They had played there since 1911.
note: MVV played at De Boschpoort from 1911 until the move to De Geusselt in 1961, confirmed.

q: When Sparta Rotterdam rebuilt Het Kasteel in 1999, what did they do to the pitch?
sub: That left the little castle along the side rather than behind a goal.
note: The pitch was turned 90 degrees in the 1999 rebuild, confirmed.

q: Ajax revealed the Johan Cruijff ArenA logo on 25 April 2018. Why that date?
sub: He would have turned 71. The Dutch spelling Cruijff was chosen on purpose.
note: Reworded. The name was announced on 25 April 2017 and only the logo was revealed on 25 April 2018, which was indeed Cruyff’s birthday. Also pulled to normal, the date is a fair guess for a regular watcher.

q: Why is RKC Waalwijk's ground called the RKC Waalwijk Stadion in European competition?
a: UEFA does not allow sponsor names on grounds
sub: PEC Zwolle's ground has to drop MAC3PARK for the same reason.
note: UEFA advertising rules confirmed on both stadium articles, PEC Zwolle drop MAC3PARK the same way. Pulled from extreme to hard, anyone who has watched a Dutch club in Europe has seen the plain name.

q: The Cambuur Stadion in Leeuwarden was demolished in 2025. In which year had it opened?
sub: SC Cambuur played there for nearly 89 years, on artificial turf at the end.
note: Opened 12 September 1936, demolished late 2025, artificial turf at the end, all confirmed. Cambuur played there from 1936 until the 2024 move, so nearly 89 years holds.

q: Ajax retired the number 14 shirt in April 2007 on Johan Cruyff's 60th birthday. What did Cruyff make of it?
a: He was against it, and said the best player should be allowed to wear 14
sub: The framed shirt went on display in the ArenA anyway.
note: Confirmed that Ajax took 14 out of use in 2007 for his 60th birthday and that Cruyff was against it, saying good players should wear the number. The exact "no honour" quote is not sourced, so the answer is softened to what is documented.

q: A housing estate stands where Ajax's De Meer used to be. What are its streets named after?
a: Away grounds where Ajax had big nights, Anfield and Wembley among them
sub: Bridges there are named after Cruyff and Rinus Michels.
note: Streets named after away grounds including Anfield and Wembley, and bridges named after Cruyff and Rinus Michels, both on the stadium article.

q: When houses went up on Ajax's old De Meer pitch, what happened to the centre spot?
a: It was recreated symbolically, because the real one was built over
sub: Ajax left the ground in April 1996 for the Amsterdam ArenA.
note: No answer a reader can judge, and it repeats the De Meer housing estate already used by the streets row. The wiki line is real but "recreated symbolically" is not something a player can produce.

q: What sits directly underneath Fortuna Sittard's stadium?
a: A multi-storey car park, with 800 spaces
sub: The ground opened in November 1999 on an old industrial site.
note: The car park with 800 spaces under the ground is on the stadium article.

q: Sparta Rotterdam's ground has a little castle with two towers behind one stand. What is it?
a: The only piece of the original 1916 stadium still standing
sub: When the pitch was turned in 1999 the castle ended up along the side.
note: The little castle is the only remaining piece of the 1916 stadium, confirmed.

q: Which Dutch club played their home matches in The Hague for months in 2019 after their own roof collapsed?
sub: They moved back into Alkmaar on 15 December 2019, against Ajax.
note: AZ played in The Hague after the 10 August 2019 roof collapse and were back in Alkmaar on 15 December 2019 against Ajax.

q: How many Eredivisie clubs played their home matches on artificial turf in 2017-18, a record at the time?
sub: Artificial pitches had been in Dutch professional football since the mid-2000s.
note: Seven clubs on artificial turf in 2017-18, a record, confirmed. Sub replaced: the seven named clubs are not verified in the source and Sparta had already gone back to grass.

q: In 2023 the Eredivisie clubs voted that from 2025-26 every club must play home matches on what?
sub: It ended about twenty years of artificial pitches in the league.
note: Vote of 5 June 2023, natural or hybrid grass compulsory from 2025-26, about twenty years of artificial pitches, all confirmed by NOS. The word unanimous is not in the source, so it is out.

q: What was built on the site of ADO Den Haag's old Zuiderparkstadion after it came down?
a: A sports campus, the Sportcampus Zuiderpark
sub: ADO left in April 2007 and demolition started that June.
note: The Sportcampus Zuiderpark on the old stadium site is confirmed.

q: Which club did FC Twente meet at the GelreDome in 2008, playing a European tie away from Enschede?
sub: They did the same in 2011 against FC Vaslui.
note: Arsenal at the GelreDome on 13 August 2008 and Vaslui there in July 2011, both confirmed.

q: ADO Den Haag laid an artificial pitch in 2013 partly with which tournament in mind for the next year?
sub: The grass came back after the 2019-20 season.
note: The artificial pitch decision was tied to the 2014 Hockey World Cup and grass came back after 2019-20, both on the stadium article.

q: Roda JC's old Kaalheide ground was never knocked down. What was it turned into from 2020?
a: Roda JC's training and academy ground
sub: The first team left it in May 2000 for the Parkstad Limburg Stadion.
note: Kaalheide became Roda's training and academy complex from about 2020, confirmed.

q: FC Twente beat Ajax 5-1 in front of 26,500 in November 1968. At which Enschede ground?
sub: It stood on the ground's record crowd, and Twente left the place in 1998.
note: Duplicate. The deck already ships "Which Enschede stadium did FC Twente leave in 1998?" and "The Diekman was the old home of which club until 1998?". Same answer, same Twente in Enschede fact.

q: Which club were the visitors for ADO Den Haag's farewell match at the Zuiderpark in April 2007?
sub: 22 April 2007, and the game was abandoned before the end.
note: FC Groningen were the visitors on 22 April 2007 and the match was stopped after 50 minutes, confirmed.

q: Roda JC's last match at Kaalheide, in May 2000, was a 3-2 win over which club?
sub: 10,000 in for the farewell on Sunday 14 May 2000.
note: 3-2 over AZ in front of 10,000 on Sunday 14 May 2000, confirmed.

q: Roda JC drew a record 24,000 to Kaalheide in September 1976 for a European tie with which club?
sub: Roda lost 3-2 in the Cup Winners' Cup.
note: 24,000 for Roda against Anderlecht on 29 September 1976, lost 3-2, confirmed.

q: NAC Breda's last league match at their Beatrixstraat ground, in April 1996, was a 0-3 defeat by which club?
sub: The farewell match followed on 12 May and the diggers moved in the next day.
note: 0-3 to Feyenoord on 28 April 1996, farewell day 12 May, demolition from 13 May, all confirmed.

q: Ajax's last match at the Olympisch Stadion, in April 1996, was a Champions League semi-final against which club?
sub: Ajax lost 1-0 and moved to the Amsterdam ArenA that summer.
note: Ajax lost the Champions League semi-final to Panathinaikos 0-1 on 3 April 1996, their last match there.

q: Homeless after their roof collapsed, AZ played a 2019 Europa League play-off at De Grolsch Veste against which club?
sub: Their league matches went to The Hague instead.
note: AZ played Royal Antwerp at De Grolsch Veste on 22 August 2019, confirmed, and their league matches went to The Hague.

q: NEC drew a record 32,000 to the Goffertstadion in 1968 for a match against which club?
sub: N.E.C. rebuilt the Goffert in 2000 on a much smaller scale.
note: Record 32,000 against Ajax in 1968 confirmed. Sub was wrong and live: the rebuilt Goffert holds about 12,650, which is nearer two fifths than a third.

q: Go Ahead Eagles packed a record 26,000 into their Deventer ground in March 1969 for a derby with which club?
sub: Four temporary stands were borrowed from the Deventer ice rink to fit them in.
note: About 26,000 against FC Twente on 16 March 1969 with four emergency stands borrowed, confirmed.

q: Ajax beat Liverpool 5-1 at the Olympisch Stadion in 1966 in a match remembered for what?
a: The fog, so thick that hardly anybody could see the game
sub: 55,722 were in, and most of them had to take the score on trust.
note: The Mistwedstrijd, 5-1, 55,722 in, confirmed on the stadium article.

q: Who struck the first blow when AZ's old Alkmaarderhout was demolished in September 2006?
a: Barry van Galen, a former AZ player
sub: AZ had played at the Alkmaarderhout since the 1967 merger.
note: Barry van Galen gave the starting signal for demolition on 11 September 2006, confirmed. Sub corrected: AZ only existed from the 1967 merger, so 1948 was not their home.

q: Fortuna Sittard's abandoned De Baandert met its end in January 2000. How?
a: Arson, which burned down the main stand
sub: The rest of the complex was flattened soon after and houses went up.
note: Arson on the main stand in January 2000 and the site cleared for housing, confirmed.

q: Which two Dutch grounds were built with a roof that slides open and shut?
a: The Johan Cruijff ArenA and the GelreDome
sub: The ArenA roof moves in two parts and takes 18 minutes to open or shut.
note: Both sliding roofs confirmed, and the Dutch article gives eighteen minutes. Sub reworded because the 520 tonnes is the roof, not each half.

q: Which English club did FC Utrecht play in the first match at the rebuilt Galgenwaard in August 1982?
sub: The old ground had closed the year before.
note: The rebuilt Galgenwaard opened on 16 August 1982 with a friendly against Southampton, confirmed.

q: What ran round the pitch at FC Utrecht's rebuilt Galgenwaard when it opened in 1982?
sub: It kept supporters off the pitch without a fence.
note: The dry moats round the pitch are on the stadium article.

q: De Kuip is a listed municipal monument. What can the city council therefore stop?
sub: The ground has been Feyenoord's home since March 1937.
note: Municipal monument status confirmed, the council has to approve demolition. Pulled from extreme to hard, the answer follows from the question.

q: Which former Ajax player lit the flame at the opening of the Amsterdam ArenA in August 1996?
sub: Johan Cruyff started the relay, with the flame carried from De Meer.
note: Rewritten twice over. The old wording gave the answer away by saying the ground later took his name, and the torch had two carriers: Cruyff started the relay, Rijkaard lit the flame. Now it asks the part with one answer.

q: Since 2005 PSV have left one seat in the Philips Stadion empty at every home match. Whose seat is it?
sub: He preferred sitting among the supporters to a box, and died in 2005.
note: Seat confirmed, vak D, row 22, seat 43, kept empty since Frits Philips died in 2005. Anchored to 2005 so it is not a live claim.

q: De Kuip's free hanging second tier, with nothing blocking the view, came to Feyenoord's president in what?
sub: Leen van Zandvliet woke up with the idea, and the ground opened in 1937.
note: Leen van Zandvliet waking from a dream with the free hanging second ring is on the stadium article, in those words.

q: What did FC Utrecht supporters do to the old Galgenwaard after the last match there in April 1981?
sub: The rebuilt Nieuw Galgenwaard opened in August 1982.
note: Supporters partly demolished the old Galgenwaard themselves after the last match on 21 April 1981, confirmed.

q: In 2009 the mayors of Amsterdam and Rotterdam agreed with the KNVB to do what to the Klassieker for five seasons?
sub: Ajax later stopped their own fans travelling to Rotterdam as well.
note: February 2009 agreement between the two mayors and the KNVB to ban away fans for five seasons, confirmed.

q: Heracles Almelo were founded in 1903 by a merger of two youth clubs. Name either of them.
sub: They started out as Hercules and changed the spelling in 1906.
note: Merger of Hollandia and Inartie on 3 May 1903, as Hercules until the 1906 spelling change, confirmed.

q: The GelreDome pitch weighs 11,000 tonnes and slides out on 16 rails. Roughly how long does that take?
sub: It parks under the south stand while the building is used for concerts.
note: 11,000 tonnes, 16 slides, about six hours, all on the stadium article.

q: Which ground held a crowd of 65,562 for a Klassieker in January 1966?
sub: Feyenoord at home to Ajax on 9 January 1966.
note: 65,562 on 9 January 1966 in Rotterdam confirmed. Pulled from extreme to hard, a serious fan works it out from the size of the crowd.

q: Ajax closed a section of their own ground in 2016 after an effigy was hung from it. Which supporters' group stands there?
sub: The F-side is the club's other famous section.
note: VAK410 closed after the February 2016 effigy, confirmed.

q: Which band played the first concert at the GelreDome, three days after it opened in March 1998?
sub: The stadium had opened on 25 March 1998, so Arnhem got the pop as well.
note: Spice Girls on 28 and 29 March 1998, three days after the 25 March opening, confirmed. Sub reworded, the twenty minute roof figure is not sourced for the GelreDome.

q: Which ground staged the Dutch Super Cup every year from 1991 until the format changed in 2017?
sub: Rotterdam also traditionally hosts the KNVB Cup final.
note: De Kuip staged it every year from 1991 until the move to the champions' ground in 2017, confirmed.

q: Which shirt number did Ajax take out of use after Abdelhak Nouri collapsed in July 2017?
sub: Nouri was 20, and suffered permanent brain damage in a friendly at Werder Bremen.
note: Ajax stopped using 34 after the July 2017 collapse at Werder Bremen, and formally retired it later.

q: Ajax renamed their Talent of the Future award in December 2018 after which young midfielder?
sub: The 2018-19 title was dedicated to him as well.
note: The Talent of the Future award was renamed after Nouri in December 2018, confirmed.

q: VVV-Venlo's ground is called De Koel. What does the word mean in the Venlo dialect?
sub: The ground was dug into an old excavation site and first used in 1972.
note: Koel is Venlo dialect for kuil, a pit, and the ground was first used in March 1972, both on the stadium article.

q: Which Dutch club has played at the Koning Willem II Stadion in Tilburg since 1995?
sub: The ground only took the king's name in 2009.
note: Willem II have played there since 1995 and the ground took the king's name in 2009, confirmed.

q: Which Dutch club's supporters call their ground De Horst, or De Vetkampstraat after the street?
sub: Officially De Adelaarshorst, in Deventer.
note: Duplicate inside this batch. Row 7 already asks which club plays at De Adelaarshorst, same answer, same ground.

q: RKC Waalwijk's old ground got a nickname from the way it looked. What did people call it?
sub: They moved out to a proper stadium in September 1996.
note: Sportpark Olympia was known as de Fietsenstalling for its looks and small size, confirmed.

q: RKC Waalwijk opened their new ground in September 1996 with a 0-2 home defeat by which club?
sub: The stadium cost seven million guilders.
note: Opened 15 September 1996 with a 0-2 home defeat by Roda JC, cost 7 million guilders, confirmed.

q: Which Eredivisie club's name is simply the French word for speed?
sub: The Arnhem founders wanted something elegant and a little bit grand.
note: Vitesse is French for speed and the founders wanted an elegant name, both on the club article.

q: Which club's supporters in Enschede have sung You'll Never Walk Alone before home matches since the 1990s?
sub: Liverpool's stadium announcer handed over the original recording in 1998.
note: Confirmed: Twente have used You’ll Never Walk Alone since the early 1990s and Liverpool’s announcer George Sephton handed over the original recording in 1998. Anchored away from "every home kick-off", which is a live claim, and the 1968 club song in the sub is not sourced.

q: Which animal rears up on the badge of FC Twente?
sub: The Saxon steed, the white horse of the Twente flag.
note: The rearing white Saxon horse of the Twente flag, confirmed.

q: The letters AZ stand for Alkmaar and which other region?
sub: The club was formed in 1967 from Alkmaar '54 and FC Zaanstreek.
note: AZ stands for Alkmaar Zaanstreek, from the 1967 merger of Alkmaar '54 and FC Zaanstreek.

q: Which bird, taken from the Arnhem coat of arms, sits on the Vitesse badge?
sub: It has survived every redesign since the club split in two in 1984.
note: The double-headed eagle from the Arnhem coat of arms, adopted after the 1984 split, confirmed.

q: Willem II's red, white and blue striped shirt takes its colours from what?
sub: Hence the nickname de Tricolores.
note: Undocumented origin. Neither the Dutch nor the English club article says the red, white and blue comes from the national flag, it is only asserted around the web. It also overlaps the shipping row on the three Willem II colours and the Tricolores nickname.

q: Which Eredivisie club was founded in 1896 as Tilburgia and renamed after a Dutch king two years later?
sub: The king had his military headquarters in Tilburg and died in the city.
note: Founded as Tilburgia on 12 August 1896 and renamed in 1898 after the king who had his headquarters in Tilburg and died there.

q: Feyenoord's club motto comes straight out of their club song. What is it?
a: Geen woorden maar daden, no words but deeds
sub: The song dates from 1961 and the official version from 1963.
note: Motto and song confirmed. Sub corrected: the song dates from 1961 with the official Jacky van Dam version in 1963, the link to the title is not in the source.

q: De Graafschap's blue and white stripes come from the colours of which town?
sub: Doetinchem lies in the Achterhoek, farming country.
note: Blue and white from the city colours of Doetinchem confirmed. Sub replaced, the story about seeing off a yellow redesign is not sourced.

q: Which Dutch club has a polar bear called Groby as its mascot, wearing number 71?
sub: The 71 is for 1971, the year the club was founded.
note: Groby the polar bear wearing 71 for the 1971 founding, confirmed.

q: Which club dropped green and white for blue and white after going bankrupt in 1990?
sub: They played as FC Zwolle from 1990 until the old name came back in 2012.
note: Bankruptcy in 1990, FC Zwolle in blue and white, PEC Zwolle back for 2012-13, all confirmed.

q: NEC's mascot Bikkel is dressed as what, in a nod to Nijmegen's history?
sub: Shield and sword included. Nijmegen was a Roman town.
note: Bikkel dressed as a legionary with shield and sword, for Roman Nijmegen, confirmed.

q: Which creature is on the FC Den Bosch badge, taken from the city's old nickname the swamp dragon?
sub: The marsh fortress held out through the Eighty Years War.
note: The badge dragon and the swamp dragon nickname from the Eighty Years War are both on the club article.

q: PSV's badge carries two stars. What does each one stand for?
sub: EST 1913 was added to the wreath in 2014.
note: Duplicate. The shipping row "Ajax’s 2011 championship was their 30th. What did it earn the club on its shirt? A third star" already teaches that one star is ten titles.

q: Where did De Graafschap's nickname de Superboeren come from?
a: An unknown supporter on the terrace in the mid-1990s
sub: The Achterhoek is farming country and the club leaned into it.
note: Unanswerable. The Dutch article says an anonymous supporter coined Superboeren in the mid-1990s, so the true answer is that nobody knows who. No single answer a player can give.

q: Go Ahead added Eagles to their name in 1971. What was the eagle taken from?
a: The eagle in Deventer's coat of arms
sub: The idea is credited to the coach at the time, Barry Hughes.
note: The eagle is the charge in the Deventer coat of arms and Barry Hughes suggested the Eagles suffix in 1971, both documented.

q: Which Dutch club has run out to an instrumental hit by The Tornados since the day it was founded?
sub: The record and the club are both named after the satellite.
note: Telstar have used The Tornados record as their run-out tune since the 1963 founding, and both are named after the satellite.

q: The G in FC Groningen's badge is drawn as a hexagon. What is that shape meant to be?
sub: A supporter, Reint Rozema, won the 1971 design competition with it.
note: Reint Rozema won the 1971 design competition and his G doubles as a football panel, confirmed. But the badge itself is a circle, it is the G that is hexagonal, so the premise is corrected.

q: ADO Den Haag play a Harrie Jekkers song after every home goal. Which one?
sub: It was never written for the club, it is the city's unofficial anthem.
note: The goal tune is the chorus of Harrie Jekkers' O, o, Den Haag, confirmed on the club article.

q: FC Twente lined up in 1965 in red shirts and white shorts. What happened to the shorts?
a: They turned red too, giving Twente an all-red kit
sub: The Twents Ros has been on the shirt since 1965.
note: Confirmed: red shirts and white shorts in 1965, the shorts became red a few years later. "Dropped" read as if they played without any, so the answer says what happened. Sub cut because the only club in one colour is a live superlative.

q: FC Emmen's badge carries a tower and six stars. Which flag are they from?
sub: The 2005 badge also restored the old red and white shield.
note: The tower and six stars of the Drenthe flag on the 2005 badge, confirmed.

q: Which Dutch club played in purple and white from 1971 until 1978?
sub: They went back to red and yellow and have not changed since.
note: Purple and white from 1971 to 1978, then back to red and yellow, confirmed.

q: Heracles Almelo swapped black and green for black and white in which year?
sub: The switch came seven years after the club was formed.
note: 1910 switch from black and green to black and white confirmed. Sub replaced, the claim about the Almelo coat of arms is not in the source.

q: When the club now called FC Emmen was founded in 1925, it went by which three letters?
sub: Nothing to do with Nijmegen. They became VV Emmen a year later.
note: Founded 21 August 1925 as Noordbarge Emmen Combinatie, NEC, and VV Emmen a year later.

q: Which Dutch club was founded in 2001 under the name FC Omniworld?
sub: They took the city's name in 2010.
note: Founded 14 September 2001 as FC Omniworld, Almere City from 2010-11, confirmed.

q: Excelsior's mascot Woutje Stein is named after what?
sub: He arrived in the 2008-09 season for the club's children's club.
note: Woutje Stein named after Stadion Woudestein and arriving in 2008-09 confirmed. The De Woudies kids club is not in the source, so the sub loses it.

q: PEC Zwolle's mascot Zwolfje is what kind of animal, and in which colour?
sub: He turned up in 2001 with the club's kids club.
note: Blue wolf, 2001, kids club, confirmed. Best mascot in the country is not sourced. Pulled from extreme to hard, the name Zwolfje points at the wolf.

q: FC Volendam's club song was written by the father of which two footballing brothers?
sub: Jan Mühren wrote Ieder kent de Volendammers.
note: Jan Muhren, father of Gerrie and Arnold, wrote Ieder kent de Volendammers, confirmed.

q: Go Ahead Eagles are nicknamed Kowet. Where does that come from?
a: It is how Deventer says Go Ahead out loud
sub: They are also called Reuzendoder, the giant killer.
note: The English article calls Kowet a Dunglish pronunciation of Go Ahead, so the origin is documented rather than folklore.

q: Which Dordrecht club played in green in the early 1990s because those were their sponsor's colours?
sub: The sponsor was a sealant maker, Den Braven.
note: Dordrecht'90 played in green because those were the colours of den Braven Sealants, the chairman's firm, confirmed.

q: Almere City put a bird of prey on their badge in 2011. Which animal's head did it replace?
sub: The club are still nicknamed the Black Sheep.
note: The sheep’s head being replaced in 2011 is confirmed, but the Dutch article says the new bird is a kiekendief, a harrier, not a kestrel. Premise reworded to a bird of prey so the row does not carry the wrong species.

q: FC Volendam are nicknamed de Palingboeren. What does that mean?
sub: Another nickname, Heen en Weer, is the boat the promoted players ride.
note: Palingboeren and the Heen en Weer boat both confirmed on the club article. Pulled from extreme to normal: for a Dutch watcher this is a translation, not an anorak fact.

q: A Sparta Rotterdam supporter revived the club's canary tradition in 1953. What did he take to matches?
a: A real live canary in a cage
sub: Frans Heijster brought the bird. It was later replaced by a woollen one.
note: Confirmed with one correction: Frans Heijster revived the Sparta-Piet tradition in 1953, he did not begin it, the cartoon canary goes back to the 1920s. Reworded to say revived.

q: PSV's club song is sung at every home match at one exact moment. When?
sub: For 1913, the year the club was founded.
note: The 19 minutes and 13 seconds tradition is confirmed on the English club article. The claim that the club motto comes from verse one is not sourced, so it is out of the sub.

q: Vitesse's yellow and black striped shirts were a gift from a baron in 1907. What was his condition?
a: That Vitesse would play in yellow and black forever
sub: Baron van Pallandt. They were the Gelderland colours, and his family's.
note: Corrected. Vitesse went yellow and black in 1900, but the striped shirts were the baron’s gift seven years later, in 1907, with the condition that they play in those colours forever.

q: From 2010 a live bald eagle flew a lap of the GelreDome before Vitesse home matches. What was he called?
sub: Falconers from De Valk Roofvogels looked after him.
note: Hertog II, an American bald eagle, has flown the lap since 2010, confirmed. But this was a live fact that has already turned: Omroep Gelderland reported the eagle no longer flies in the GelreDome, so it is put in the past tense and anchored to 2010.

q: PEC Zwolle's fans are the Blauwvingers, the blue fingers. What is the legend behind it?
a: Zwolle sold Kampen its bells and counting the copper coins turned their fingers blue
sub: Historians say it is nonsense, and that blauwvinger meant an oath-breaker.
note: Both halves check out: the bell and copper coin legend, and the historians' verdict that blauwvinger meant an oath-breaker after Zwolle swore to Karel van Gelre in 1520.

q: Excelsior of Rotterdam are nicknamed the old paper club. Why?
a: A chairman collected waste paper for years to keep the club alive
sub: Henk Zon, the chairman who kept the club out of bankruptcy.
note: Chairman Henk Zon and the waste paper collecting confirmed. The 1977 single is not in the source, so it goes.

q: De Graafschap's mascot is a zebra called Guus. Who is he named after?
sub: Hiddink played for and managed De Graafschap.
note: Zebra Guus is named after Guus Hiddink, who played for and managed the club, confirmed.

q: Where did the boys who founded Go Ahead in December 1902 get the money to start the club?
a: They pooled their Sinterklaas money and bought a ball
sub: They called it Vooruit first, then Be Quick, then Go Ahead in 1905.
note: Documented after all, and not just folklore: the club history and the Canon van Nederland both say the Deventer boys bought a ball with their saved Sinterklaas money in December 1902. Answer tightened to what the sources say, that the money bought the ball.

q: Which sportswear brand's kit did Ajax start wearing in 2000?
sub: Their previous supplier had been on the shirt since 1989.
note: Adidas from 2000 confirmed, but "has made since" is a live fact and the 2031 extension is not in the source, the listed deal runs to 2025. Rewritten as a dated event, and the sub avoids naming Umbro because another row asks for it.

q: Which car maker was on Feyenoord's shirt from 1984 to 1989, and came back from 2013 to 2017?
sub: In between came HCS, Stad Rotterdam, Fortis and ASR.
note: Opel 1984 to 1989 and again 2013 to 2017, with HCS, Stad Rotterdam, Fortis and ASR in between, all on the sponsor table.

q: Which bank's name was on Ajax's shirt from 1991 until 2008?
sub: They took over from the cassette tape maker TDK.
note: ABN AMRO 1991 to 2008, taking over from TDK, confirmed.

q: Which cable and internet company became Ajax's shirt sponsor on 1 January 2015?
sub: Aegon had carried the shirt since 2008.
note: The Ziggo deal began on 1 January 2015, taking over from Aegon who had it from 2008.

q: Which Japanese car maker was FC Utrecht's first shirt sponsor, staying for about ten years?
sub: The black lines in the club badge went blue in 1983 to match Nissan.
note: Nissan as first sponsor for about ten years confirmed, and the badge going blue in 1983 to match Nissan is on the club article. The exact start year is disputed, kit archives say 1982 and the Dutch article says shirt sponsorship arrived in 1983, so the year is out of the question.

q: Which bank and insurer was on Feyenoord's shirt from 2004 to 2008?
sub: It became Fortis ASR and then ASR Verzekeringen.
note: Fortis 2004 to 2008, then Fortis ASR and ASR Verzekeringen, confirmed.

q: Which Rotterdam insurer was on Feyenoord's shirt for thirteen years from 1991?
sub: The same firm briefly gave its name to Excelsior's ground.
note: Stad Rotterdam Verzekeringen 1991 to 2004, and the same firm did give its name to Excelsior's ground.

q: Which Schiedam health insurer became Excelsior's main sponsor in 2004?
sub: From 2017 DSW handed its place on the shirt to charities.
note: DSW became Excelsior’s main sponsor on 7 May 2004, confirmed, but the old claim fails: from February 2017 DSW gave its place on the shirt to charities, so it was not on the shirt in 2017-18. Rewritten to the dated event.

q: Which insurer replaced ABN AMRO on Ajax's shirt in 2008?
sub: They stayed until Ziggo took over at the start of 2015.
note: Aegon replaced ABN AMRO in 2008 and stayed until Ziggo came in at the start of 2015, confirmed.

q: Which English brand made Ajax's kit through the 1990s, including the 1995 Champions League win?
sub: They supplied Ajax from 1989 until Adidas came in for 2000.
note: Umbro from 1989 to 2000, so through the 1995 Champions League win, confirmed.

q: Which brand made PSV's kit for twenty years from 1995?
sub: Adidas had it from 1974 to 1995, then Umbro followed Nike in 2015.
note: Nike 1995 to 2015, Adidas 1974 to 1995, Umbro from 2015, confirmed.

q: Which insurer was sc Heerenveen's main shirt sponsor for about fifteen years, up to and including 2015-16?
sub: After that they moved to the back of the shirt.
note: Unive were on the chest from 2001-02 until 2016, about fifteen years, and moved to the back and sleeve afterwards.

q: The Dutch second tier was the Jupiler League until 2018. What name did it take then?
sub: Before Jupiler it was the Gouden Gids Divisie.
note: Jupiler League 2006 to 2018 and Keuken Kampioen Divisie from 2018 confirmed. "Since 2018" was a live phrasing, so it is anchored to the change itself.

q: Which brand supplied Go Ahead Eagles' kit for more than thirty years, from 1988 to 2020?
sub: Stanno took over in the summer of 2020.
note: Hummel from 1988 to 2020 confirmed, but the count was wrong: the club celebrated thirty years in 2018-19 and the sources say a thirty-one year partnership, not thirty-two seasons.

q: Which insurer's name was on FC Utrecht's shirt from 1992 to 2005?
sub: Nissan had it for the ten years before that.
note: AMEV from 1992 to 2005, with Nissan the ten years before, confirmed by the kit archives.

q: Which phone book gave the Dutch second tier its name from 2001 to 2006?
sub: The same brand had been Feyenoord's first shirt sponsor in 1982.
note: Gouden Gids Divisie from September 2001 to June 2006, and the Gouden Gids was Feyenoord's first shirt sponsor in 1982.

q: Which energy company was on Feyenoord's shirt from 2017 to 2019?
sub: They were there for the 2018 KNVB Cup win.
note: Qurrent 2017 to 2019, so on the shirt for the 2018 cup win, confirmed.

q: Which textile firm was Heracles Almelo's main shirt sponsor from 2003 to 2016?
sub: The same company made the artificial pitch they played on.
note: Ten Cate were Heracles’ main sponsor from 2003, not from 2007-08, and Asito took over in 2016. Years corrected. The artificial pitch link is right, TenCate Grass supplied it.

q: Which zoo was on NEC's shirt in 2017-18?
sub: Before them came EnergieFlex and Scholten Awater.
note: Ouwehands Dierenpark in 2017-18, EnergieFlex 2016-17, Scholten Awater 2013-14, all confirmed.

q: AZ ran out against NAC in August 2010 with what printed on the front of the shirt?
sub: Their sponsor DSB had gone bust and no replacement had been found.
note: AZ played NAC on 8 August 2010 with a large question mark on the shirt after DSB went under, confirmed.

q: Which sportswear brand took over PSV's kit from Umbro in 2020?
sub: Nike had it for the twenty years before Umbro.
note: Puma took over from Umbro for 2020-21 when the Umbro deal expired on 1 July 2020, and Nike had the twenty years before.

q: Which Eredivisie club has a mascot called Storky?
sub: Stork is simply the English for ooievaar. His partner is called Stricky.
note: Storky the stork and the female mascot Stricky are both on the club article.

q: Which two colours does the FC Utrecht home shirt use, taken from the city arms?
sub: Red shirt with white shorts has been the look since the late 1970s.
note: Red and white from the Utrecht city arms, confirmed.

q: Which Eredivisie club has a tiger called Sibi as its mascot?
sub: He arrived in 2010 for the Red White Tigers children's club.
note: Sibi the tiger and the Red White Tigers kids club, from late 2010, confirmed. Moved off easy: nobody outside Emmen can name that mascot, so easy was the wrong shelf.

q: Which Dutch club was founded in 1920 under the name Victoria?
sub: The name changed to Volendam in 1923, when the orange shirt arrived.
note: Founded 1 June 1920 as Victoria and renamed Volendam in 1923 with the orange shirt, both confirmed. The founders being local fishermen is not in the source, so that comes out.

q: Which television broadcaster's name was on FC Volendam's shirt from 1990 to 1994?
sub: Veronica were a household name on Dutch television then.
note: Veronica on the Volendam shirt from 1990 to 1994 confirmed by the kit archives. The later sponsors in the sub are not verified, so they go.

q: Which Italian brand made Feyenoord's kit from 2000 to 2009?
sub: Puma followed, then Adidas from 2014.
note: Kappa 2000 to 2009, Puma to 2014, Adidas from 2014, confirmed.

q: Which gym chain's name was on ADO Den Haag's shirt from 2012 to 2017?
sub: Cars Jeans put its name on the shirt and on the ground after them.
note: Basic-Fit 2012 to 2017 confirmed. Sub reworded: Cars Jeans took the stadium name in 2017 and the shirt only in 2018, so "took over both" was too neat.

q: NAC Breda brought back their original 1912 badge for the centenary in 2012. Who paid for it?
sub: A black shield with a yellow diagonal band and the letters N.A.C.
note: NAC brought back the 1912 crest for the 2012 centenary and kept it on supporters' initiative and donations.

q: Which travel company's name was on NAC Breda's shirt when they finished third in 2007-08?
sub: Sunweb were on the NAC shirt from 2005 to 2012.
note: NAC did finish third in 2007-08, and Sunweb were on the shirt, but the sponsorship ran from 2005 to 2012, not for the four seasons stated. Anchored to the season instead.

q: Which Japanese electronics brand was on FC Groningen's shirt from 1987 to 1996?
sub: Nine seasons with the same name on the shirt.
note: Pioneer from 1987 to 1996 confirmed on the club article. The list of sponsors before and after is not in the source, so the sub is replaced.

q: Which clothing firm was Go Ahead Eagles' first shirt sponsor when advertising was allowed in 1982?
sub: They came back for a second spell in 1987.
note: Piet Zoomers of Wilp were the first main sponsor in 1982, confirmed on the club article.

q: Feyenoord's sponsor handed its shirt slot to a Rotterdam attraction for half of 2012-13. Which one?
sub: ASR gave up the space from January to June.
note: ASR gave its shirt space to Diergaarde Blijdorp from January to June 2013, confirmed on the sponsor table.

q: Which Japanese electronics company was AZ's first shirt sponsor, from 1982 to 1986?
sub: Shirt sponsorship arrived in Dutch football in 1982-83.
note: Sony as AZ’s first shirt sponsor from the 1982-83 season confirmed on the club article. The three names that followed are not sourced there, so the sub changes.

q: Which holiday park chain became PEC Zwolle's main shirt sponsor in 2015?
sub: They had been on the back of the shirt since 2012 and stayed to 2021.
note: Molecaten became main sponsor in 2015, confirmed, but they stayed until 2021, not 2019. Anchored to the start instead of a wrong span.
